segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
This is a night for when you have lost someone. [pause 10]

Get as comfortable as you can. You can let the phone rest beside you. [pause 12]

Tonight is Psalm 23. Many people first hear it at a funeral, and come back to it on the long nights afterward. [pause 12]

We will read it twice. You only need to listen. [pause 12]

verses.text: A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.
Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
The psalm does not go around the valley. It goes through it, one step at a time. [pause 15]

And in the middle of the valley, the words change. David stops talking about God and starts talking to him. Thou art with me. [pause 15]

That is often how grief prays. Not in long sentences. Just, you are here. Stay with me. [pause 15]

There is a table in this psalm, and a cup, and a house to come home to. You do not have to feel any of that tonight. It is there in the words, waiting for you. [pause 15]

Two more short passages now. [pause 12]

verses.text: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Blessed are they that mourn. Jesus said that about people standing exactly where you are. Mourning is not failing. [pause 15]

And Paul gives God two names you can hold tonight. Father of mercies. God of all comfort. Comfort for this, too. [pause 15]

Now Psalm 23 again. Let it go slowly. Let each line land before the next one comes. [pause 15]

verses.text: A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.
Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
That is enough for tonight. [pause 8]

Let your shoulders drop. Let the bed hold you up. [pause 12]

You may be thinking of their face, or their voice, or the last time you spoke. You can hold that gently. [pause 15]

Grief is a kind of love. It is all right that it hurts. [pause 15]

You do not have to carry it alone. A pastor, a grief counselor, a friend who will sit with you: these are good gifts, and it is good to ask for them. [pause 15]

The Lord is with you in the valley. Stay here as long as you like. [pause 30]

Good night. [pause 45]

first_reader.note: Drafted and read by Claude in the landing session; no free-model draft (QA_NO_FREE_MODEL not needed).

pastor.note: Grief nights and the 3 AM night (21 Nov 2026): every passage is stored KJV pasted by code (Ps 13, Ps 23, John 11:32-36, Ps 4:8 and companions); written lines echo in short phrases only. Lament is allowed (How long) without rebuke; no reason given for a death, no 'better place', no timeline for grief (the grief_words check); Rev 21:4 told as the hope at the end of the story, not a claim about the person who died; Jesus's and God's words given indirectly outside scripture. Each grief night points to a pastor or a grief counselor; the 3 AM night makes no sleep promise.

cultural.note: Plain, unhurried English a grieving or half-awake listener can follow at 3 AM; the person who died is 'them', never assumed to be a spouse, parent or child; no pity, no hurry ('nobody is timing you'); the 3 AM night is short and spare, the phone face down. Lengths by silence only: grief nights 10-11.5 min, the 3 AM night 6 min (estimated at 117 wpm).
